key_insight: Autonomous Science Bench tests whether AI agents can choose experiments, learn from limited lab feedback, and deliver useful scientific models under a strict budget.
engineering_relevance: For materials discovery workflows, the benchmark helps distinguish agents that explore well from those that generalize well, which is critical for efficient autonomous experimentation.
method: Six budgeted design-build-test-learn campaigns based on published biology, chemistry, and materials experiments
Agents pick batches of designs and receive measurements from a lab service over multiple rounds
Performance is judged by two gates: discovery on measured designs and learning on held-out design ranking
evidence_signal: In 144 pilot trials across eight agent-model configurations, the best setup succeeded in 67% of trials, while the hardest campaign was solved only 3 times out of 24 attempts.
watch_item: Because the benchmark is currently version 0.1 and based on a limited set of six campaigns, results may not fully generalize to all autonomous discovery settings.
paper_title: Autonomous Science Bench: Evaluating AI Agents for Autonomous Scientific Discovery
